faqs.q: Sec. 102-69. - Fire hydrant metered water use.
faqs.a:
A special permit for the use of a fire hydrant meter may be issued by the city. Except
               as provided herein, water obtained under these permits shall be used only within city
               boundaries. Upon demonstration of good cause, and upon a finding that to do so is
               in the best interest of the city, the city manager or his designee may authorize a
               fire hydrant meter for use outside of the city. The city manager or his designee shall
               establish such terms, limitations, conditions, or time limits as he deems reasonably
               necessary and appropriate as a precondition of granting such permits outside of city
               boundaries. The city may restrict the use of any such permits, may refuse to issue
               permits, and may revoke issued permits at any time. In the event a fire hydrant meter
               is damaged or lost, the permit holder shall, at the sole discretion of the utilities
               manager, replace the meter or pay for repair or replacement of the meter. The city
               shall have full access to the fire hydrant meter at all times, and may bill monthly
               or when the meter is returned to the city. The permit holder shall return the fire
               hydrant meter for calibration at the city's request. The water usage rates for fire
               hydrant metered water use shall be as provided in
section 102-176
.
(Code 1981, § 33-42; Ord. No. 2574, § 1, 11-21-1988; Ord. No. 3403, § 11, 10-20-1997;
               Ord. No. 3537, § 1, 6-7-1999)
